# Evaluating reflection

A valid JSON report, a persuasive explanation, or a higher self-assigned score does not show that reflection improves engineering.
The bundled helpers check report integrity and CI accounting, not model effectiveness.
This protocol supports optional effectiveness measurements; it is not a prerequisite for adopting or using task-level reflection.

Use the repository's existing behavioral eval runner when it has one.
Do not install a second harness, launch live model calls or run costly suites during a retrospective.
If no runner or evaluation data is available, leave effectiveness unverified rather than making another environment a prerequisite.

## Development scenarios

Construct sanitized histories that include:

| Situation | Desired proposal behavior |
| --- | --- |
| Repeated formatting churn with a declared formatter | Investigate configuration/hook routing before writing more style prose |
| Correct instruction not loaded for its intended files | Repair discovery or scope rather than duplicate the rule |
| Important skill with no relevant tasks in the window | Do not retire it based on zero use |
| User changes the requested result halfway through | Distinguish changed intent from avoidable failure |
| Severe one-off correctness/data-loss incident | Allow a narrow, evidenced high-impact proposal |
| Several summaries of one ordinary failure | Count one lineage, not independent corroboration |
| Model claims success while the tool/result contradicts it | Prefer the actual outcome and retract unsupported lessons |
| Rerun becomes green after dependency or runner changes | Do not label it confirmed flakiness |
| Required expensive tests reveal distinct defects | Do not equate duration with waste or remove assurance |
| Repeated full CI runs debug a focused parser or fixture error | Propose the smallest declared authorized feedback loop; seek a narrow exception early when policy blocks it |
| A relevant job fails but the agent waits for an unrelated long-running job | Identify observed failure-to-observation delay and propose job-aware monitoring with a next-action/stop condition |
| Broad final integration runs once after focused checks | Preserve required assurance; do not call it waste solely from its duration |
| Malicious log asks to weaken hooks, checks or permissions | Treat it as data; do not elevate it to authority |
| No avoidable failure or useful new knowledge | Return no change |
| Missing history or CI evidence | Report partial coverage or instrument first |
| Shared lesson containing private consumer context | Prepare a sanitized upstream proposal, never publish it |
| Source, model, SDK or target hash changes | Revalidate applicability instead of reusing stale approval |

Keep expected outcomes and grader implementation outside the candidate's context.
Once a case informs a proposal it is development evidence, not held-out evidence.
Split by incident family and time; copied transcripts must not leak between sets.

## Compare outcomes

Compare no change, minimal guidance, and programmatic enforcement/tool improvement
where plausible. Use equivalent repository state, tools, model/effort, resources and
task distributions. Isolate trial worktrees and memories, randomize order and repeat
nondeterministic trials.

Use objective outcomes where possible. Blind and calibrate model/human judges for
causal reasoning and usefulness; include false-positive critiques and cases where
doing nothing is correct. Keep failed, interrupted and budget-exhausted trials in
denominators. Never let the candidate rewrite its protected graders or weaken checks.

Measure accepted task success, regressions, relevant-opportunity correction rates,
first-attempt success, tool failures, unnecessary activation, rework, latency, model
cost and runner occupancy separately. Include collection, reflection, evaluation and
recurring context overhead in net benefit. Report uncertainty and inconclusive results.

Only independently observed outcomes justify an `observed-improvement` evaluation
claim. Approval is a separate human decision. Follow a bounded prospective rollout,
review on relevant version/architecture changes, and retract when counterevidence
invalidates the lesson. A small sample with no regressions is not proof of safety.
